papers.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
summary_bullets: Virtual Tissues is a foundation model for analysing spatial proteomics across different marker panels and experimental protocols.
It aims to transfer tissue knowledge across cohorts instead of requiring a separate model for every study.
The framework supports tissue representation and biomarker discovery across spatial scales in cancer datasets.

papers.title: A spatial code governs olfactory receptor choice and aligns sensory maps in the nose and brain
summary_bullets: The study links olfactory receptor choice to the spatial organization of sensory neurons in the nose.
This spatial receptor code helps align peripheral sensory organization with corresponding maps in the brain.
The work connects cell-fate choice, tissue position, and neural circuit organization.

papers.title: RegVelo: Gene-regulatory-informed dynamics of single cells
summary_bullets: RegVelo combines single-cell RNA sequencing with prior gene-regulatory knowledge to infer regulatory dynamics.
It models transcription as a regulated process, capturing coupled gene behavior during cell-state transitions.
Integration with CellRank enables in-silico perturbation experiments and cell-fate prediction.

papers.title: A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models
summary_bullets: The study expands the Cancer Dependency Map with next-generation three-dimensional cancer models.
The models capture vulnerabilities that conventional two-dimensional cancer cell lines can miss.
The resulting resource supports systematic target discovery and precision-oncology research.

papers.title: A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers
summary_bullets: The resource assembles next-generation patient-derived models across a broad range of cancers.
It addresses gaps in existing model collections that represent only part of human tumour diversity.
The compendium supports therapeutic testing and validation of cancer disease mechanisms.

papers.title: A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies
summary_bullets: The study builds a tumour-derived organoid biobank linked to patient and cancer context.
Three-dimensional organoids complement cell lines by better representing tumour diversity.
The biobank enables systematic mapping of cancer gene dependencies for research and drug discovery.

papers.title: Generative design of bacteriophages with genome language models
summary_bullets: Genome language models generated complete bacteriophage genomes rather than individual genes or proteins.
Experimental testing produced viable phages with diverse sequences, structures, and fitness profiles.
A mixture of generated phages overcame bacterial resistance to a natural bacteriophage.

papers.title: Recovering signatures of archaic hominin introgression using ancestral recombination graphs
summary_bullets: TRACE identifies archaic ancestry from ancestral recombination graphs without requiring an archaic reference or unadmixed outgroup.
It recovers known Neanderthal and Denisovan ancestry and detects signals from uncharacterized hominins.
The method enables mapping of archaic introgression even when archaic genome sequences are unavailable.

papers.title: Hallmarks of cancer—Then and now, and beyond
summary_bullets: The review revisits how the hallmarks-of-cancer framework has evolved since its original formulation.
It assesses established and emerging capabilities that support tumour development and progression.
The updated perspective considers how the framework can guide future cancer research and therapy.

papers.title: Hallmarks of Cancer: The Next Generation
summary_bullets: The review organizes cancer biology around core capabilities acquired during tumour development.
It adds deregulated metabolism and immune evasion as emerging hallmarks of cancer.
Genome instability and tumour-promoting inflammation are described as enabling characteristics.
